sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion (£1.34 trillion).
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: The artificial intelligence (AI) company's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Anthropic's shares flew past its allocation price of $83 each , showing there was plenty of excitement around AI.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Yet the company, which is behind AI chatbot Claude, will remain under intense scrutiny in the months ahead to answer the key question surrounding AI: is it all worth it?
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: In just a few hours of trading, Anthropic's stock seemed to show that investors remain uncertain of where exactly AI is heading.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: The share price rose immediately to $111.53, sending the company's market value to almost $2 trillion, before falling by the end of the day as the shares closed at $97.17.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Some investors said Anthropic's debut seemed to be a success, as shares rose roughly 17% during the day, but the broader tech market did not perform as well.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index closed down nearly 2.3%.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Stocks fell in the largest tech firms, including Google's parent company Alphabet, which was down by 2.9%, while Amazon lost almost 3.9%.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: The buildout happening around this era of AI is among the most expensive endeavours in the history of technology, with more than $1 trillion being spent in the last year alone by a handful of major tech companies.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: The speed at which investment has grown has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: "Bubbles don't burst on the day of the largest deal," Richard Whittle, an economist with the University of Salford said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: The result has been AI chatbots that simulate human speech and operate tasks like software coding, digital image generation, and searching the internet more quickly.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: It represents a new way of using computers that has led to the rapid rise of Anthropic, which started just five years ago and is best known as the maker of the popular AI chatbot Claude.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: As the first purely AI company to go public, Anthropic will almost certainly see significant swings in price on the stock market going forward, according to Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: The "initial exuberance" will wear off, Barringer said, pointing to what happened with SpaceX earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: That company, led by Elon Musk, saw shares jump by about 10% on the first day of trading, taking the company to a record-breaking valuation of $2.2 trillion.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Within a month shares had fallen below their debut price, and have mostly fallen further since.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: But many such companies, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: With Anthropic, investors are not only looking at a notable tech company with a major valuation, and a potentially big future in business, but a company that is the first of its kind on the stock market.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: "There's no obvious peer to compare it to," Neil Wilson, an investor strategist at Saxo UK, said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Simon Jack: Can Anthropic's record-breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: So, as individual investors and even researchers and investors at large funds ask themselves if Anthropic is really worth more than $1.7 trillion, or even more, there will be few answers available.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: "We'll have a stab at it," Wilson said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: "I don't think anyone really knows." A few things will likely impact the company's success on the stock market in the near-term.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: One of those things is the prospect of new laws governing the use of AI tools.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: In the US, where Anthropic is based, Democrats will be in many more positions of power come 2027, and several politicians have already said they will be looking to ensure AI tools are safe and have some guardrails attached.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Such regulation is currently unlikely at the federal level.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: US President Donald Trump on Thursday spoke about AI during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, alongside Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: A significant driver of this kind of scrutiny is Anthropic itself.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Company executives, including co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei, have been outspoken in their purported fears that future AI tools will become so capable they will outsmart humans, to the point where extinction is possible.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Anthropic has always put itself forward in public as an AI company that takes the safety of its technology very seriously.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Daniela Amodei, Anthropic's president and sister of Dario Amodei, boasted on Thursday that the company "had an AI safety team before we launched our first product".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: "AI carries real risks," she added.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut

sentences.text: Despite the company's claims that the technology it is building at a rapid pace could be dangerous, Anthropic has made one of the quickest trips from start-up to IPO in history.

sentences.text: Recent waves of cyber-attacks in Europe have seen tonnes of food spoiled at hundreds of stores, causing millions of pounds of damage.
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: France has blamed Iran for one of the waves of attacks that impacted its supermarkets, a claim Tehran denies .
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: It was thought the UK had largely escaped such hacks as the British refrigeration industry relies on different devices but there was in fact a potential vulnerability the sector has been rushing to fix.
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: In late October, security researchers discovered a major flaw that, if found by hackers, could have led to even worse damage to the UK.
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: Since then, researchers, IT teams and the National Cyber Security Centre have been working around the clock to warn dozens of companies.
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: The BBC has not reported on the large-scale, secretive operation until now to reduce the chances of hackers causing harm if they found the vulnerability.
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: The security threat was discovered by ethical hackers at a firm called Omega Systems - it was then verified and expanded upon by experts at Pentest Partners who helped raise the alarm.
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) and Food Standards Agency (FSA) were then involved in the campaign to plug the security holes.
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: They held industry conference calls and tasked teams to contact firms at risk.
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: Thousands of devices controlling tens of thousands of refrigeration devices were taken off the open internet either remotely, or in some cases, physically - with staff ordered to remove internet cables and monitor temperatures manually.
sentences.article_title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

sentences.text: Marwa was pregnant and new to the UK when her father died in Egypt We're all going to die - and whether we think about it consciously or not, we generally hope that it will be as smooth as possible for ourselves and our loved ones.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: But a study published earlier this year by King's College London and the University of Sheffield suggests that your ethnicity could play a role in how likely this is to be the case.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: The research found that people from minority ethnic backgrounds experiencing end-of-life care and grief often struggled to access culturally and religiously appropriate support.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: One woman told researchers a hospital sent an Imam - a Muslim religious leader - to her father's bedside when he was dying, even though their family were Hindu.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: That lack of culturally appropriate resources or training is exacerbating an "incredibly difficult time in their lives where they were really vulnerable", says Sabrina Bajwah, one of the study's co-authors.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: So how can our ethnic or cultural background shape what kind of death we have?
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: And what kind of support is available?
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: Bajwah told the BBC researchers discovered different types of inequality in their research.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: "There was the structural racism that people talked about, which was the 'treating everybody equally' - and by treating everybody equally, services weren't meeting the needs of these communities," she said.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: "Then there was the other, direct form of racism." A study last year from the NHS Race and Health Observatory, set up in 2021 to try and tackle racial inequalities within the wider healthcare system, found there was an "alarming" lack of trust among some ethnic minority groups in the care or service they receive.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: For example, just over half of participants said they had experienced some form of discrimination from their healthcare providers.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Department of Health and Social Care, which commissioned this year's study, told the BBC that "ethnicity or background should never be a barrier to accessing bereavement support and everyone has the right to the same level of care".
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: "We will consider the findings of this research project carefully as part of future policy making," they said.

sentences.text: But pledges of further "dialogue" and an acknowledgement that nuclear war "must never be fought" provide minimal substance beyond the rhetoric.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: "In general, it's good for the leaders of the major global players to come together in various formats, even if the results appear to be modest at best," David Firestein, head of the Bush Foundation for US-China Relations, told the BBC.

sentences.text: And it was hard to miss the condemnation of the International Criminal Court – a recent target of American ire.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: While in China, Trump called Putin his "friend", and praised his "outstanding personal relationship" with Xi after sharing a handshake and hug with the Chinese leader.

sentences.text: But once Trump returns to Washington, he is likely to face a political environment where views of his Asia trip range from measured concern to outright criticism.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: "I am concerned by how we are characterising our relationships with geopolitical adversaries.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are not our friends," Republican Senator John Curtis of Utah said in a statement to the BBC on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: "Diplomacy is important, but it should never come at the expense of clarity about who our adversaries are." sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: But he adds that Putin is a "dictator" and "an international criminal".
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: "He invaded a sovereign, independent, democratically-elected country, and continues to engage in aggression there." Democrats, for their part, did not mince words.

sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: Trump is hardly the first American president to seek an international diplomatic breakthrough as a salve following domestic political setbacks.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: Democrats Bill Clinton and Barack Obama took overseas trips as presidents shortly after their party's own midterm electoral defeats.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: In those cases, any boosts to their standing proved short-lived.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

sentences.text: The Dutch privacy watchdog, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP), has told people not to buy smart glasses, saying they can get things dangerously wrong.

sentences.text: It said in its tests of six glasses available on the Dutch market, the devices advised a user on how to date a child, misread medicine instructions, and claimed to have called an ambulance when they had not.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: While the AP is advising people not to buy the smart glasses, it stopped short of calling for them to be banned from sale.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: The authority is not revealing which glasses it tested, saying only that prices ranged from under €100 (£84) to over €500 and originated from different continents.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty of all eight counts against him in a Florida court on Wednesday A Florida pastor has been found guilty of a number of charges relating to the assassination of the Haitian President Jovenel Moïse.
sentences.article_title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president

sentences.text: Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a dual US-Haitian national, was convicted of all eight charges against him, including conspiracy to kill or kidnap a person.
sentences.article_title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president

sentences.text: He faces a potential sentence of life in prison.
sentences.article_title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president

sentences.text: The 67-year-old was accused of being involved in a plot to replace Moïse as Haiti's president with himself in 2021, allegedly so he could award lucrative contracts to a Florida-based security outfit once in place.

sentences.text: The murder of Moïse has left Haiti without a leader for five years.
sentences.article_title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president

sentences.text: That political vacuum has intensified gang violence in the impoverished Caribbean nation.
sentences.article_title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president

sentences.text: Sanon was found guilty on Wednesday following an eight-week trial in federal court in Miami, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner.
sentences.article_title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president

sentences.text: His lawyer said he maintains his innocence and that he intends to appeal against the verdict, it reports.

sentences.text: Prosecutors said Sanon had "political aspirations" in Haiti and, in April 2021, met several other co-conspirators to devise a plan to oust Moïse in an armed raid on the presidential palace in the capital, Port-au-Prince.

sentences.text: Among them were the heads of the companies Counter Terrorist Unit Federal Academy and Counter Terrorist Unit Security - collectively referred to as CTU - who would finance the coup in exchange for government contracts for infrastructure projects, and to provide security forces and equipment.

sentences.text: A few months later, the other conspirators realised that Sanon had "neither the constitutional qualifications nor the popular support" to become Haiti's president and so shifted to another candidate, the US Department of Justice said.
sentences.article_title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president

sentences.text: At the same time, the plot had developed from one to forcibly remove Moïse from office to assassinating him, investigators said.
sentences.article_title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president

sentences.text: Dozens of people have been implicated in the conspiracy, which prosecutors said involved co-ordinating funding for and delivering weapons and mercenaries to Haiti to carry out the attack.
sentences.article_title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president

sentences.text: Elon Musk said on Wednesday that he felt "pretty foolish" about the record sum he spent on the US midterm elections, following sweeping Republican defeats.

sentences.text: "This money can employ over 100,000 nurses and 200,000 teachers," an X user posted.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: But the government has rejected the criticism, saying Ghana's economic circumstances have changed considerably since the NDC opposed a similar purchase.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: Peter Lanchene Toobu, chairman of parliament's defence committee, said the party had never opposed acquiring a presidential jet in principle.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: Its objection, he said, had been on the timing when Ghana was experiencing severe economic difficulties.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: "We agreed in principle that we needed to purchase a new presidential jet," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: He argued, however, that Ghana could not justify the expenditure at a time when it was seeking a $3bn bailout from the IMF.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: "The strength and macroeconomic stability of this country have enhanced our status in the sense that imports have become cheaper, and this is the right time," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: Toobu said the government had purchased the aircraft without borrowing, citing a stronger Ghanaian currency and improved economic conditions.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: Government spokesperson Kwakye Ofosu also dismissed suggestions that the purchase was a misplaced priority.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: He pointed to falling prices of construction materials and lower borrowing costs as evidence of the country's improved economic situation.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: "When I was campaigning in 2024, and I was donating cement, it cost 115 cedis (£7.5) a bag.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: Today, for 80 cedis, you will get a bag of cement," he told JoyNews.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: The controversy has also extended to the aircraft's interior, following claims that it has a dedicated bedroom and bathroom.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: But Ofosu dismissed claims that the jet had such luxury facilities, saying the president has no intention of "bathing in the air".
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: "There certainly is no bathroom.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: President Mahama has no intention of bathing in the air," Ofosu said.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: He explained that the jet has reclining seats that can be converted into sleeping arrangements but denied that it has a dedicated bedroom.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: The government says the new jet will replace the 16-year-old Falcon 900EX, which has suffered recurring maintenance problems, including corrosion and leakages in its fuel tank.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: The older jet was reportedly grounded in France for several months in 2025 while undergoing repairs.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: Officials say the Falcon 6X has a longer flying range, reducing the need for refuelling stops on international trips and improving the reliability of presidential travel.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: Professor Godfred Alufar Bokpin, an economist at the University of Ghana said that while the president's safety was paramount, the timing of the purchase was difficult to justify amid severe austerity measures, high unemployment and widespread infrastructure challenges.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: "The timing makes it a bit difficult to understand," he told the BBC, adding that the government should provide a cost-benefit analysis explaining why buying the jet was preferable to leasing one and how the decision serves Ghana's interests.
sentences.article_title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

sentences.text: Early efforts to contain coronavirus "were doomed to fail" because the test, trace and isolate system in the UK could only handle a relatively small number of cases, the seventh report of the Covid inquiry says in a damning assessment.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Across 245 pages the inquiry looks at everything from border controls to how well contact tracing worked.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report said the virus was allowed to spread virtually unchecked in the first few months after community testing and contact tracing was abandoned in mid-March 2020, costing lives.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers said this was because testing capacity was being overwhelmed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: NHS Test and Trace was launched two months later and eventually became one of the biggest testing services in the world per head of population.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the end, more than £30bn was spent across the UK during the pandemic on testing, tracing and isolating.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Once established, it was effective.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But in those early months the four UK nations were "effectively blind" to how quickly Covid was spreading, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It criticises the government for not having a robust test, trace and isolate system in place to start with, saying this, alongside other failures, meant harsher measures, including lockdown and school closures, were needed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Inquiry chair Baroness Hallett said the UK should have been better prepared and learnt lessons from other countries that had experience of dealing with outbreaks of other infectious diseases, such as Sars.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Unlike the UK, places such as Hong Kong, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan had established systems ready to go.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: This was despite the fact the UK had run a series of simulation exercises in the years leading up to Covid.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: They included Exercise Cygnus into a flu pandemic and Exercise Alice into Mers.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Both identified problems relating to test, trace or isolation, which appear not to have been fully acted on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report also raises the question of whether the government could have made use of non-government testing facilities in hospitals, universities and the private sector from the start, instead of just relying on 12 government labs.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: When people in the UK were told to isolate, "many felt forgotten and let down by the lack of practical or financial support when trying to follow the rules", says the report.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the early months of the pandemic, estimates suggested less than half of people were complying with the rules around isolating if infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers and their advisers discussed this and fines of up to £10,000 were introduced for those who did not comply, which some experts have said was counter-productive.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Changes were made to allow people to claim statutory sick pay.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But it was not until September in England – and later in Scotland and Wales – that £500 financial payments were introduced to help those on low incomes comply.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: More also needed to be done to provide practical support for things such as collecting medicines and shopping for food for those who did not have people to call on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Suspending all flights from China to the UK in February 2020 could "have provided valuable additional time to prepare healthcare systems for the impact of the pandemic", said inquiry chair Baroness Hallett.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says the UK lacked a clear strategy for implementing border control measures early in the pandemic, which left the country in an "extremely vulnerable position".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: By contrast, the UK government only requested travellers arriving from high-risk areas to self-isolate for 14 days.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The UK government implemented no further border control measures until June 2020.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says that border controls were a "critical gap in the UK's ability to limit the spread of the virus" and recommends that in the future "international border control measures should be in place at the earliest stages of a pandemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry report is more positive about the use of smartphone apps, saying digital tools can have a "significant impact on reducing the spread of infection".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes a mathematical modelling study from the US which estimates that, when 75% of people used a contact tracing app in the pandemic, infections were reduced by at least 50%.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Three different apps were developed during Covid - one for England and Wales, another for Scotland and a third for Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry says that took up "valuable time", and it recommends developing a UK-wide digital tool to use in any future outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It says it is "fundamentally important" that apps and digital tools are as accurate as possible – and people have confidence in them.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the summer of 2021, as Covid restrictions were relaxed, around 7% of all UK adults were told to self-isolate over a seven-day period, something dubbed by the press as the "pingdemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes Treasury estimates suggesting that may have reduced economic growth by as much as 0.3% that month.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Significant damage was caused to the left eye of the sculpture A man has been jailed for five months after causing an estimated £10,000 worth of damage to Belfast's Big Fish sculpture.
sentences.article_title: Tourist jailed for damaging Belfast's Big Fish

sentences.text: Peter Smith, 44, of no fixed abode, admitted criminal damage and possessing items with intent to damage property.
sentences.article_title: Tourist jailed for damaging Belfast's Big Fish

sentences.text: He is believed to have used a hatchet, a hammer and a sledgehammer to smash ceramic tiles around the sculpture's left eye.
sentences.article_title: Tourist jailed for damaging Belfast's Big Fish

sentences.text: District Judge Francis Rafferty told Belfast Magistrates' Court: "I regard it as a targeted attack, but it remains unexplained." Police were called to Donegall Quay shortly after midnight on 20 September.
sentences.article_title: Tourist jailed for damaging Belfast's Big Fish

sentences.text: A witness saw Smith striking the sculpture with a long-handled object and detained him until officers arrived.
sentences.article_title: Tourist jailed for damaging Belfast's Big Fish

sentences.text: Smith was carrying a hammer and a small hatchet in his backpack and officers later found a sledgehammer in nearby bushes.
sentences.article_title: Tourist jailed for damaging Belfast's Big Fish

sentences.text: Defence barrister Garrett O'Kane said Smith was visiting Belfast from England and that he had a psychiatric disorder following a car crash four years earlier in which two of his sons were killed.
sentences.article_title: Tourist jailed for damaging Belfast's Big Fish

sentences.text: O'Kane said Smith told him that he had found the tools and used them to attack the sculpture.
sentences.article_title: Tourist jailed for damaging Belfast's Big Fish

sentences.text: The court heard that plans for repairing the sculpture remain unclear.
sentences.article_title: Tourist jailed for damaging Belfast's Big Fish

sentences.text: Glamping site owner Carol Esteban is appealing a court ruling of £135,000 in legal costs A glampsite owner is challenging a court order to pay £135,000 in legal costs after she tried to block her neighbours from parking their car in their own garden.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: Carol Esteban told her neighbours Neil and Nadine Gould that their right to use their shared driveway ended opposite their front door, which would block them from their parking space.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: Both sides accused the other of trespassing, while Esteban was accused of using "boulders" to block the couple's access to the shared track.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: The Goulds sued Esteban in 2025 and won a High Court ruling enabling them to drive far enough along the track to turn off into their parking space.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: But Esteban has now appealed that ruling.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: In the ruling in July 2025, Judge Milwyn Jarman explained how the Goulds' detached cottage, Cwmtawe Villa, Abercrave, near Swansea, was completely surrounded by land attached to Cwmtawe Farm, where Esteban runs her glamping site, which was set over 60 acres of ancient woodland with their own individual hot tubs.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: The properties were once all held by the same owner, but the house was sold off in 1949, with documents relating to that transaction now lost.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: However, a 1964 conveyancing document stated the owners of Cwmtawe Villa could enjoy an "easement" - granting them the right to use a track owned by the farm to access their house on foot or with vehicles.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: But a missing letter on a map attached to the document sparked the row over how far along the track the easement ends.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: Esteban argued that a thick hedge had surrounded the villa at the time the right of way was granted and that it would have "made no sense" for the right of way to entitle the owners to go any further than the gap in the hedge by the front door.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: But Jarman rejected Esteban's argument, and said her assertion "has the potential to lead to impracticability, if not absurdity".
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: He concluded that the claimants were entitled to a declaration that their vehicular right of way extends to the space at the north side of the villa, where they currently park their vehicles.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: Esteban was also handed a £135,000 costs bill.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: Cwmtawe Farm houses glamping pods set in 60 acres of ancient woodland with their own individual hot tubs Appealing the ruling at London's Court of Appeal, Daniel Bromilow, representing Esteban, said the High Court judge did not come to his decision by interpreting the 1949 plans.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: He argued Jarman had determined what he thought the parties should have agreed to in relation to the right of way, and said there was "no evidence" the track shown on the plan extended beyond the front door of Cwmtawe.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: He also argued against Esteban being handed her neighbours' cost bill for the case, saying she had "succeeded to a significant extent on her counterclaim", including winning a claim that a new waterpipe had been installed unlawfully on her land by the couple.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: Owen Curry, representing the couple, urged the appeal judges to uphold the decision, saying the judge had "reached the right conclusion in the case".
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: The judges have reserved their decision on the appeal, to be given at a later date.
sentences.article_title: Glampsite owner appeals £135k bill after blocking neighbours from using their driveway

sentences.text: Archaeologists spent a month digging at Sutton Hoo in 2025 A mysterious "sand body" has been uncovered during renewed excavations at Sutton Hoo.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: The site, near Woodbridge in Suffolk, is renowned for its royal burial ground and ship burials that have transformed historians' understanding of medieval England.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: Now, yet more mysteries have been uncovered after the television archaeology series Time Team returned for a special dig in 2025, which has now been chronicled in a four-part documentary season.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: These include an Anglo-Saxon grave and evidence of a second burial site beneath it, as well as beads, tweezers, a knife and a brooch.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: Angus Wainwright, from the National Trust, and Helen Geake, who is part of Time Team The excavations, which took place over the course of a month, were carried out in Garden Field, a separate cemetery from the site's famous royal and 7th Century ship burial grounds.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: Angus Wainwright, an archaeologist with the National Trust, said the latest dig put the focus on normal people and their ancestors and descendants.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: "Until now, archaeologists have focused on the royal burial mounds," he said.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: During the recent excavation, the team uncovered one of the site's sand bodies, made when a long-decomposed body leaves behind a ghost-like shape almost like a fossil.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: "It was certainly a high point of this latest dig, to find another of these bodies in the Garden Field cemetery," added Wainwright.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: The National Trust said the discoveries raised further questions about the size, chronology, and character of the cemetery Another major focus of the investigation has been the Bromeswell Bucket, a rare Byzantine artefact discovered at Sutton Hoo.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: Following the recovery of missing fragments during Time Team's first season in 2024, the team returned to investigate its contents and piece together its story.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: Dr Helen Geake, Time Team's Anglo-Saxon specialist, said she was "thrilled to finally locate and excavate the burial" but there were "still many questions to answer".
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: "What date is the bucket?
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: What lay behind the choice of cremation and inhumation on this part of the site?" she said.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: "And what is the significance of the inhumation grave with its tantalising hint of another below?" This was the main trench that was opened up by the team during the 2025 dig The findings are being revealed in the four-part seeries which are being aired on YouTube throughout November.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: They raise further questions about the size, chronology, and character of the Garden Field cemetery, and how it fits into the wider story of Sutton Hoo.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: Tim Taylor MBE, Time Team creator and series producer, said returning for a new series in partnership with the trust made for some "fascinating discoveries".
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: "As ever with archaeology, the more we uncover, the more questions we find ourselves asking," she said.
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: "That's exactly what makes it so exciting, and I can't wait for everyone to see what the team has been up to." Do you have a story suggestion for Suffolk?
sentences.article_title: Anglo Saxon 'sand body' among new Sutton Hoo finds

sentences.text: Photonic chips use light instead of electrons to process data "Photonic chips are on the verge of a breakthrough," says Ton van Mol of the Dutch research institute TNO.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If van Mol is right – and TNO, the European Union and the Dutch government are backing the idea with millions of euros - then the technology could be a gamechanger.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The chips which run today's society, from your phone and TV, to the vast data centres meeting our insatiable desire for AI, are mostly electrical.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: They process data by shunting electrons around tiny circuits – a single microchip produced today can contain billions of transistors, and sizes are measured in nanometres (one nanometre is a billionth of a metre).
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Van Mol hopes for an acceleration in photonics similar to the one seen in electrical chips since the 1970s.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "With optical chips, you are now where electronic chips were maybe 40 [or] 50 years ago." American, Taiwanese and Chinese firms dominate the computer chip industry, but Europe sees the emergence of photonic chips as a fresh opportunity to lead, on what could be, a key future technology.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why the European Union has committed €400m ($450m; £330m) to a project called PIX Europe , external , with the stated goal of making the continent "a global leader in emerging technology for Photonic Integrated Chips".
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe said 'we need to have our own manufacturing in-house'," says van Mol, who is leading a key part of the programme.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Factories with machines that can handle bigger wafers can churn out chips more efficiently.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "[Photonic chip] manufacturing worldwide is [currently] done on wafers which are four inches (10cm) in size, and the next step is to scale-up production to a six-inch wafer," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: His team are already building a 10,000 sq m factory to produce six-inch indium phosphide wafers on the High Tech Campus in the Dutch city of Eindhoven.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's due to fully open in 2030 and will be a major step forward, not just for photonics in Europe, but around the world, according to van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "That's the development TNO is going to do, in a pilot line which is really serious.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The Netherlands-based tech giant is the only company in the world able to build the machines needed to make the most sophisticated semiconductors.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why ASML products will sit at the heart of the pilot line in Eindhoven - it's no coincidence that van Mol's project is based around the corner from ASML's headquarters.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "The way you produce these [photonic] chips is very similar to the way you produce electrical or electronic chip," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "You use the same type of equipment, you also need a high-end clean room, you also use wafers, so the production method is very similar to the traditional semiconductor technology." ASML itself is keen to explore the opportunities that the emerging technology of photonics could offer.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe has a strong position in photonics research.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The next challenge is translating those innovations into industrial-scale manufacturing," says Stanislas Baron, who is the head of ASML's EU/US Customer Team.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The Eindhoven project has the backing of former ASML chief executive Peter Wennink, author of an influential report for the Dutch government called The Roadmap to Future Prosperity , external , which noted that the market for photonics was expected to grow 10 to 20 times in the next 10 years.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: In a news release backing the new pilot line, Wennink described it as "a launchpad for Europe's future digital economy".
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "By investing in scalable production capacity, we are creating an ecosystem that can help shape the global technological direction," he said.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Of course, Europe is not alone in looking to the potential of photonics to earn a global economic advantage.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: In June this year, US photonics company Coherent announced what it called "the world's first and largest volume-production six-inch indium phosphide manufacturing platform" at its plant in Sherman, in Texas.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The expansion is backed by chip manufacturing giant Nvidia , external , as well as $50 million public funds under the US Chips Act.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's an illustration of how quickly the market is moving, and how central photonic chips could be to the continuing race to retain an influential stake in AI and technological development more generally.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Europe's bid to establish itself as a global leader in photonic chips – exemplified by the Eindhoven project – is the kind of strategy that makes sense in a globalised economy, says Joris Teer, policy analyst at the European Institute for Security Studies in Brussels.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If the continent can take a lead in photonic chips, then future developments in AI and data will partly be dependent on Europe.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe knows that its high energy and labour costs, skilled workforce shortages, and lack of private and public capital make an across-the-board reindustrialisation strategy impossible", Teer says.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "To retain influence, ensuring dependence on European parties rather than European autonomy is key." Once up and running, the Eindhoven project will provide a pilot production line which can be used multiple companies.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It will be open to businesses across Europe and beyond, who can design and build chips without having to develop their own expensive production facilities.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "What we want to establish here is what we call a foundry model; there's no intention to have our own product," Ton van Mol says.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Instead, they will produce to order for outside customers.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Does the theory really know more about us than our own lived experience of a 10-year marriage?
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: The five love languages are: Quality Time, Acts of Service, Words of Affirmation, Receiving Gifts, and Physical Touch - and they feel more ubiquitous than ever.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: Contestants on dating shows ask each other their love languages; "My love language is…" is a common prompt on dating apps.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: According to the Love Languages website, my husband and I are just two out of more than 150 million people to have taken this particular quiz.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: Even though we scored much lower on some of the other languages, they speak more directly to us.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: For example I love spending "quality time" with my husband, and feel much more loved by him making lists of films to watch with me than when he pays me a compliment.

sentences.text: But where did the idea of these five neat categories come from?

sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: Chapman said the theory came to him after observing couples during counselling sessions he held in his parish.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: Counselling psychologist Dr Sarah Emmerson told the BBC that love languages are still mentioned regularly in her sessions.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: "There's almost no-one out there who hasn't taken that quiz," she said.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: "[Couples] quite frequently bring that in and say, 'So my partner is Physical Touch and I'm Acts of Service, so this doesn't work'.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: "Research has proven that there isn't a lot of validity to the idea that there are only five ways in which people show love, and that everybody fits neatly into these categories.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: But people still gravitate towards it, and we have to wonder why that might be." Fan edits have tried to guess the love languages of Nick and Charlie in Heartstopper For some, talking about love languages can simply be a useful introduction to thinking about how they communicate their needs to their partner.

sentences.text: Psychotherapist Georgina Sturmer said that it helps people think about "what you really like in a relationship, and what do other people really like" but points out it's "hugely limited" and risks "oversimplifying everything".
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: In recent years, many therapists have also warned that Chapman's examples refer too readily to scripture and unequal relationship dynamics.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: In the Love Languages book Chapman describes counselling a woman, Ann, whose husband of 10 years is hostile and verbally abusive towards her, including frequently telling her he hates her.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: His love language, Ann tells Chapman, is specifically sexual physical touch.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: When Ann says she finds it "hard to be sexually responsive" to him, Chapman advises her that she should "rely heavily upon [her] faith in God" to make herself have sex with her husband more often.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: This example also exposes another problem - that love languages can be used to coerce partners into showing or receiving love in a way they're not comfortable with.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: "There's a risk if someone says, 'well my love language is receiving gifts, so you must give me gifts all the time, or my love language is physical touch, so you must be physically intimate with me all the time," Sturmer said.

sentences.text: The BBC has contacted the Love Languages team for comment.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: Chapman's theory of love languages is 35 years old but is often still mentioned by couples So what can couples do if they want to understand each other, and themselves, better?
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: Share how you feel using "I" statements, so you avoid blame: "If you reframe your words to lead with your own feelings, it helps you to express what's going on without leaving the other person feeling criticised," Sturmer explained.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: Remember that disagreements are normal: "Healthy relationships often feature debate and disagreement," Sturmer said.
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: "The challenge is not about avoiding rupture, it's about finding ways to repair it that can leave the relationship feeling stronger." But, Dr Emmerson added, you should "pick the right time to talk about things that are difficult - not late at night, not when they've just come through the door".
sentences.article_title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?

sentences.text: The trial was funded by the US, under Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has a long record of expressing scepticism about vaccines.

sentences.text: The proposed trial drew international criticism because it planned to withhold a vaccine recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) from half of the participating newborns.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Some public health experts argued that the proposed trial raised broader questions about whether vulnerable populations in African countries were being asked to take risks that researchers would not accept in wealthier countries.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The BBC has asked the US department of health and human services for comment.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Here is what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The study was planned at the Bandim Health Project, a research centre that has operated in Guinea-Bissau since 1978.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: It was designed to involve 14,000 newborns, with half receiving a hepatitis B vaccine shortly after birth and the other half not being given the shot .
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Bandim said the trial aimed to investigate whether the hepatitis B vaccine given at birth has broader health effects beyond preventing infection.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Previous studies in The Gambia and Guinea-Bissau have raised questions about a possible link to increased mortality.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Researchers argued that because Guinea-Bissau does not currently offer routine hepatitis B vaccinations at birth, despite WHO recommendations, they have a unique opportunity to study its effects before such vaccines are introduced in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: But critics questioned the ethics of withholding the vaccine from some babies, particularly in one of the world's poorest countries, where the infection is widespread.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The Trump administration funded the proposed study, with the CDC awarding the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) $1.6m (£1.2m) in December 2025 .
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Walter Kazadi Mulombo, the WHO representative in Guinea-Bissau, told the BBC they became concerned after receiving questions about the study and finding no publicly available protocol.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: He said the main ethical concern was that the trial would withhold an intervention already proven to protect newborns against hepatitis B.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "The vaccine has been used for more than 30 years in more than 115 countries," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "A study that will withhold that intervention from other newborns is unethical." He warned that babies could be exposed to the virus during childbirth if their mothers were infected, as well as later in life.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Nearly a fifth of the population of Guinea-Bissau are infected with hepatitis B, a viral infection that affects the liver.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Those infected during infancy are particularly likely to develop chronic infections, which kill up to 25% of people, mostly through liver failure or liver cancer, according to data published in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The WHO is working with the government to bring forward the birth-dose vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "The country had been expected to add it to its routine immunisation schedule in 2028, but officials are considering introducing it in the first quarter of next year," Mulombo said.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Guinea-Bissau currently vaccinates children against hepatitis B at six weeks, which means it is less effective.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Guinea-Bissau's government prohibited hepatitis B vaccine trials involving children in January.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Health Minister Quinhin Nantote said in October that the suspension remained in force and had not been overturned by the Council of Ministers after reports emerged claiming that the trial would be taking place after all.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "We were surprised to learn from media reports that the study might proceed," Nantote said.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "We are outraged because even I, as the minister responsible for this sector, was not informed." The dispute intensified after the SDU said a revised study protocol had received ethical approval "from the relevant authorities in Guinea-Bissau", which Nantote denied.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Dr Gavin Yamey, a professor of global health and public policy at Duke University in the US, criticised the proposal.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "The proposed trial reeks of neocolonialism," he told the BBC, questioning why the research was not being conducted in Denmark.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: His criticism centred on the decision to withhold a recommended vaccine from some newborns in a country where hepatitis B is widespread.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: SDU dean Jakob Grauslund said the trial had never started, no babies had been enrolled and no vaccinations administered as part of the research.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The SDU said it had received a separate, positive assessment from the university's own research ethics committee.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: He added that the relevant Danish statutory research ethics bodies were unable to undertake the review.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Following the approval from the SDU's ethics committee, Grauslund decided that the project could proceed.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: He, however, stressed that this did not replace the separate authorisation required from Guinea-Bissau's authorities.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: On 19 October, Guinea-Bissau's Judicial Police searched the Bandim Health Project's facilities in the capital, Bissau, and seized a batch of hepatitis B vaccines.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Police said the batch was intended for vaccinating children but did not disclose how many doses had been seized or the specific grounds for the investigation.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: They stressed that the seizure did not, in itself, mean the vaccines were defective or unsafe.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The police have not explicitly said whether their investigation relates to the proposed trial, the importation of the vaccines or other circumstances surrounding the batch.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Grauslund said he could not comment on the seizure of the vaccines.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The proposed trial was funded by the US government at a time of significant changes to vaccine policy under President Donald Trump and Health Secretary Kennedy.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Under Kennedy's leadership, a US vaccine panel attempted to end a longstanding recommendation that all newborns receive a hepatitis B vaccine at birth, but a federal judge later blocked this, along with other changes to vaccine policy made by the Trump administration.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Critics have questioned whether the research could help support that policy shift, although the study's stated aim was to investigate potential effects of the vaccine beyond preventing infection.

sentences.text: Kennedy has praised the Danish researchers as "the deities of vaccine research", and cited earlier findings from their work in support of concerns about vaccine safety.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau
