sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.

sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.

sentences.article_title: Rare rhino's first steps captured on video at zoo

sentences.text: The video shows 19-year-old mother Asha with her newborn calf at their enclosure after Asha had been pregnant for 15 months.
sentences.article_title: Rare rhino's first steps captured on video at zoo

sentences.text: Keepers said both rhinos were in good health and the birth was an important step in the conservation of the threatened species.
sentences.article_title: Rare rhino's first steps captured on video at zoo

sentences.text: Tom Garland from the rhino team at Chester Zoo said the calf was the fourth born to Asha and father Beni, who died earlier this year following a short and sudden illness.
sentences.article_title: Rare rhino's first steps captured on video at zoo

sentences.text: "It's always exciting to welcome a new calf and Asha has been a brilliant mum to all her youngsters," he said.
sentences.article_title: Rare rhino's first steps captured on video at zoo

sentences.text: The calf is part of a Europe-wide conservation breeding programme that helps to maintain a healthy and genetically diverse population of greater one-horned rhinos in human care.
sentences.article_title: Rare rhino's first steps captured on video at zoo

sentences.text: Conservation scientist John O'Hanlan said supporting Asha's 15-month pregnancy had been "really exciting".
sentences.article_title: Rare rhino's first steps captured on video at zoo

sentences.text: "She's one of relatively few greater one-horned rhinos in Europe actively breeding, so every successful birth is important in maintaining a healthy and genetically diverse population," he said.
sentences.article_title: Rare rhino's first steps captured on video at zoo

sentences.text: The birth is part of a Europe-wide conservation breeding programme Mark Brayshaw, Head of Mammals at Chester Zoo, said in addition to safeguarding the genetics of the species, Asha and her calf could also help millions of zoo visitors understand the value of conservation.
sentences.article_title: Rare rhino's first steps captured on video at zoo

sentences.text: "Greater one-horned rhinos are much better protected in the wild than they once were, but many of them are concentrated within one national park in India, which makes them vulnerable to illness and environmental changes," he said.

sentences.text: The legal action against Natural Resources Wales landed in the High Court River campaigners are taking on Wales' environmental regulator in the High Court over what they believe is a "regulatory gap" that risks pollution from poultry farms in two rivers.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: River Action UK has accused Natural Resources Wales (NRW) of not doing enough to assess or address any risk to local rivers and and other water bodies when plans for three farms in Powys were approved last year.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: It follows years of debate over the alleged impact of chicken farming on rivers such as the Wye and Severn - in an area dubbed the UK's "poultry capital" .
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: NRW said it would be inappropriate to comment ahead of the court case, but that it would "participate fully in the legal process".
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: The case is about plans to increase the capacity of three Powys farms by a combined 336,900 chickens, bringing the total to 522,000.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: The three farms are Neuadd Isaf, Rhosddu and Llanshay.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Two of the farms, Rhosddu and Llanshay, are in the River Severn catchment while Neuadd Isaf is in the River Wye catchment.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Campaigners said the Severn was showing "signs of strain" with regular algal blooms, brown algae smothering the riverbed.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: The three poultry units in Powys are located within river catchments including the River Wye Campaigners' concerns have centred around the birds' manure becoming a pollutant when it is spread on fields and leaches into rivers.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Nutrient-rich agricultural run-off can contribute to algal blooms, turning rivers green and smothering wildlife.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Following a consultation, NRW approved permit variations in November 2025, allowing the three poultry units to expand.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Rather than keep and spread the manure on site, the farms' operators said they would export it for use or processing elsewhere.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: River Action argued NRW wrongly concluded it had no legal power under the Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016 to assess the potential environmental impacts of this off-site manure management, or to take action to prevent or mitigate pollution arising from it.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Emma Dearnaley, head of legal at River Action, argues there is a "regulatory gap" in the management of off-site manure Campaigners set up a chicken-themed protest outside the High Court hearing in Llandrindod Wells on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: The organisation insisted NRW could put controls on the farm's permit to reduce or remove the risk of manure causing pollution.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Campaigners believe the birds' manure will spread on fields and into rivers, causing harm Emma Dearnaley, head of legal at River Action, said NRW "decided that it didn't have the power to look at what would happen when a lot of the manure would go offsite" when the plans were approved in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: "That matters because more chickens means more muck, and that needs to go somewhere and someone has to deal with it," she said.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: "So this case is all about making NRW realise that it does have the power to deal with it." An NRW spokesperson said: "As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment on matters that are before the court.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: The Jackdaw platform is located 150 miles east of Aberdeen Gas has begun flowing from the Jackdaw gas field, with the UK energy secretary saying it will help to heat millions of homes and businesses this winter.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: Ministers last month announced the Jackdaw field, which lies 150 miles east of Aberdeen, had been approved after years of uncertainty and a court case.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: It has now been announced that it has begun producing gas which will start flowing into Britain, according to its operator Adura.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: The UK government approved production from the gas field in the North Sea last month, amid intense debate about the project's environmental and economic impact.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: Miliband says he won't resign if government approves Rosebank oil field Burnham defends Jackdaw decision as Badenoch urges PM to overturn ban on new oil and gas licences Jackdaw is operated by Adura under a joint venture between Shell and Norwegian state energy firm Equinor.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: A decision is yet to be taken on whether production can begin at Rosebank, the UK's largest known untapped oil field, which is located off the coast of Shetland in the North Atlantic.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said: "Last month, I gave Jackdaw the green light and today its gas will start flowing into Britain, thanks to the hard work of the skilled North Sea workers.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: "It means homegrown gas from this project will help to heat millions of British homes and businesses this winter and beyond, in a boost for our energy security.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: "It also will help minimise the UK's use of imported higher emission gas as we continue our transition to renewables and nuclear." Claire Mueller, Jackdaw project director at Adura, said the gas field was "now helping to power Britain".
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: She added: "At a time of considerable uncertainty around the world, Jackdaw will provide secure energy from our own waters to heat British homes and power our economy, while reducing our reliance on imports with higher emissions.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: "Jackdaw also demonstrates what can be achieved when Britain makes pragmatic, evidence-led decisions about the energy it needs, while properly accounting for our climate responsibilities." Mueller said the decision was a "positive step towards restoring confidence in the North Sea".
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: She added that Adura was "proud to be producing the oil and gas our country will continue to need for decades".
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: After imports are included, that amounts to about 2% of total UK demand.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: The gas will be pumped to the existing Shearwater platform for processing – known as a tie-back in industry terms – before being piped to the St Fergus gas terminal in Aberdeenshire.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: The UK government said that over its expected 11-year lifespan, Jackdaw would support the UK's gas supply, protect hundreds of jobs and add £2.9bn to the economy.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: The decision to green-light Jackdaw drew criticism from some Labour backbenchers and environmentalists, while Conservatives called on the government to also approve the Rosebank oil field.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: Both projects were approved for development by the previous Tory government in 2022 and 2023 respectively but these decisions were struck down by the Scottish courts after a challenge from environmental campaigners.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: This followed a Supreme Court ruling that developers had to account for the climate impact caused by burning fossil fuels in their planning applications.
sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.article_title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light

sentences.text: He said: "It is a devastating betrayal of our children's future and it won't even lower energy bills in the here and now." Environmental campaigners argue that this summer's heatwaves demonstrate the need to tackle climate change by rejecting both Jackdaw and Rosebank.

sentences.text: Outages and IT failings are commonplace - but not on this scale.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: In the past week, there has been a massive Microsoft outage , an apparent tech glitch which grounded all US flights for hours , and issues for the National Security Agency (NSA).
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: That's not to mention outages affecting the biggest US banks , as well as a major flaw found in a popular programming language .
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: These are all separate incidents - but the fact they have all come so close to each other has got people wondering if they might be linked.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: There is no evidence to suggest this - but they do tell us a lot about how the modern tech world works, and where the vulnerabilities lie.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: As is often the case, many outages were a result of an update or installation going wrong somewhere in a system.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: A network upgrade at Microsoft caused servers to become overloaded and shut down.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: It was also upgrades to a creaky old network which grounded thousands of planes in the US over the weekend.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Problems with the NSA's internal communication system and, separately, Apple's iCloud and Apple Pay were also blamed on things going wrong during system updates.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Disruption to payments in US banks has been put down to a "software bug" from JP Morgan Chase.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: The bank says it is not a cyber-security incident.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: But some recent problems are in fact related to cyber-security vulnerabilities.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: AI was used to discover flaws in Java, the third-most popular programming language in the world.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: And researcher Scott Helme also discovered malicious code in Optimizely, a platform which is used by some of the world's largest companies.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Hackers were able to steal about $7,000 (£5,300) in cryptocurrency before they were discovered and kicked out.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Let's address the cyber incidents first - and the role of new AI models.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "I would be very surprised if all of these cyber-attacks and the attackers behind them were not using AI to accelerate themselves," Helme told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Since the summer, AI companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI have decided it's too risky to give the general public access to the most advanced models before allowing certain companies and institutions to use them.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: In these cases, security professionals can use the same tech to find flaws themselves and alert others before criminals get to them.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: This happened in the recent Java incident , as well as the PHP one - where there was a scramble to patch the flaws before they could be exploited.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Then there are the outages.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: These are not new - the world stood still in recent years as CrowdStrike and then Amazon Web Services ground many devices and systems to a halt.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Part of this may be down to technical debt - a term used when operators go for quick fixes to software instead of solving an underlying problem.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: A build-up of surface-level fixes can eventually end up with more serious problems down the line.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: With AI causing many companies to re-evaluate their cyber-security, they may be issuing more updates to patch flaws they have found.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Outages are often also a reminder of the physical tech our online world relies on - such as cables, servers and data centres.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: In the US air traffic control incident, for example, the problem came as engineers were replacing outdated copper wires with fibre.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is adamant the recent incidents are not connected or coming from one attacker.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "We are not under systemic attack," he said.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "These events, one has nothing to do with the other, they are not inter-related." In cases such as PHP and Java, the "good guys" found the flaws, with the help of AI, before the bad guys - allowing them to get together some fixes before the bugs could be widely exploited.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: At the same time, Anthropic, among other leading AI firms, has warned of the risks its own products pose .
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Outages in particular have an impact on the physical world as they often cause disruption to healthcare, schools and people's ability to do their jobs.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Or, in the case over the weekend, planes' ability to fly.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Marco Rubio says recent tech outages are 'completely unrelated' to one another They also shine a light on the world's heavy reliance on a small number of players.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Not just frontier AI companies, but infrastructure providers such as Microsoft and Amazon, which - along with Google - run a huge chunk of the world's computer servers.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: In the PHP incident, the world was holding its breath as one programmer - working voluntarily - worked to issue patches in a form that was easily applicable.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: And Java, run by another tech giant Oracle, is used by nearly all of the biggest companies on Earth.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "The Oracle Java vulnerability is a stark reminder of how dependent businesses have become on a relatively small number of critical technologies," said Sheila Pancholi, risk assurance lead at consultancy firm RSM UK.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "Organisations need to know where their critical technology dependencies sit, act quickly when vulnerabilities emerge, and test that their response has actually worked." Meanwhile Xander Van Raemdonck, security engineer at Aikido Security, said the challenge was "knowing whether you're exposed".
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "Java is bundled inside a huge amount of business software, so many companies don't have a full list of where it runs," he said.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: The AI tools used to help find security flaws are still so new that they will probably continue to find vulnerabilities which have been lingering in code for decades.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "AI is accelerating discovery on both sides and speeding up how much software gets shipped," said Martin Reynolds, field CTO at software delivery company Harness.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "So the volume of what developers need to patch is going up, while the time they have to get the work done it is going down." Tech debt will need to continue to be dealt with - which means more upgrades to systems and more potential for these to cause disruptions.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Plus there is the constant threat from hackers as they continue to get more sophisticated.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Attackers only need to find one vulnerability to exploit - whereas defenders have to protect against all potential hacks.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "Attackers can move quickly and carefree, and experiment without risk of failure so they can naturally often move a fraction faster," Helme said.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "We're currently observing that small delay between how fast the attackers can move and how fast the defenders can move." The cat-and-mouse nature of the cyber-security game means it's unlikely to end any time soon - and the impact of AI means the stakes are getting higher.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket for the first time, after a flight lasting 22-and-a-half hours.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: The rocket returned to Earth and hovered near its launch tower, whose mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - then secured it.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: The company had hoped to catch the bottom part of the rocket as well, but this was aborted a few minutes after the launch on Friday.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: SpaceX needs to reliably recover both parts of Starship so that it can fly repeatedly and drastically reduce costs.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: The moment the rocket came back to Earth The Starship rocket launched successfully on Friday There were loud cheers from SpaceX staff who were watching the flight as the rocket returned to the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: This is the 15th test of Starship and the first that hoped to fully recover both parts of the rocket.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: SpaceX wants to make the top and bottom sections of Starship fully reusable.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: The 124m-tall (407ft) rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 16:47 local time (19:47 GMT) on Friday.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: The plan was to grab the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six-and-a-half-minutes later when it returned.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: But the booster activated an automated abort, diverting instead to the ocean where it hovered above the water before exploding.
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: Elon Musk later posted on X that the booster had been "slightly low on fuel".
sentences.article_title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time

sentences.text: The lower stage of the rocket was diverted to the ocean and burst into flames The top part of the rocket continued its journey to space where it deployed 26 satellites, which form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet.

sentences.text: But this was the first time the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has been grabbed by the "chopsticks".

sentences.text: "These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.
sentences.article_title: Shevchenko accuses Mudryk camp of 'baseless slander'

sentences.text: "The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case.
sentences.article_title: Shevchenko accuses Mudryk camp of 'baseless slander'

sentences.text: We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.
sentences.article_title: Shevchenko accuses Mudryk camp of 'baseless slander'

sentences.article_title: Shevchenko accuses Mudryk camp of 'baseless slander'

sentences.text: I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism.
sentences.article_title: Shevchenko accuses Mudryk camp of 'baseless slander'

sentences.text: "If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it.

sentences.text: Adam Abbou stars as Freddie in the hit BBC series This City Is Ours With millions of viewers and a major role in a Bafta-nominated series, you might not expect Adam Abbou to know much about feeling self-conscious.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "When we were kids it wasn't so cool to be from Liverpool," the This City Is Ours actor says.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "I'd be in these rooms with people who were really posh and I always felt out of place." The Liverpool-based BBC series has become a hit, with Abbou, who plays Freddie, stepping into a prominent role for its second season.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: But it's not just the storylines on drugs, gangs and murders hooking audiences - it's the setting too, and the Scouse actors bringing it to life.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: Created by Liverpudlian writer Stephen Butchard, This City Is Ours recruited heavily from Merseyside.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: Lead actors James Nelson-Joyce, Jack McMullen and Mike Noble were all born in Liverpool, as was Abbou, who grew up in Anfield.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: But like many young and aspiring actors, for a long time he thought where he came from could hold him back.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "I didn't see a lot of [Liverpudlian accents] on TV when I was a kid," the 23-year-old says.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: As a result, acting "always felt really out of reach".
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: Abbou played the title role in a touring production of Billy Elliot the Musical in 2015, and has since appeared in dramas like Casualty, Time and Waterloo Road.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: He says he wasn't expecting his latest gig, where he plays Freddie, gangster Banksey's son, to become so significant.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "If you would have asked me 10 years ago, I would have said you probably need to move to London," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: While This City Is Ours provided him with his big break, he says more needs to be done across the industry to open doors.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: New research from the Creative Industries Policy and Evidence Centre , external published last week found representation of people from working-class backgrounds has fallen over the past five years, from 25% in 2021 to 21% now.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "I think it's a trust issue," Abbou says, with producers less willing to take risks on new talent.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "But if you give a working-class kid a chance they will run with it and they won't let you down." In January, the BBC committed to working harder to make sure people from different backgrounds were portrayed accurately and authentically in its output.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: It followed a report that recommended the broadcaster could improve how it represented working-class communities, highlighting how their stories often focus on "themes of poverty, crime and addiction".
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: That's true for This City Is Ours, which follows the lives of drugs gangs, with Freddie becoming more involved in the business throughout the second series.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: That portrayal of the city is something Liverpool's mayor said he wasn't happy about.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: But Abbou insists he was confident about the series' ability to represent his hometown authentically and dismisses accusations it glamourises crime.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "I was never worried because Stephen [Butchard] roots all of his writing in Liverpool," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "He is a Scouser, he knows what it's like to grow up a Scouser.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: The environment and gorgeous scenery of the city is always embedded in the script.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "It's a show that paints the city in a wonderful light.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: Of course the characters are flawed, but that's the nature of the show that we're creating." Abbou was thrilled to be trusted with a more prominent role in the second series From the reaction he's had locally, Abbou thinks the series has been a boost for Liverpool overall.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: The reaction has been "quite crazy" in the city, he says, "but of course it would be because people love to see themselves and their accent reflected on TV and when it is, you almost feel like you know the person".
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "It has truly been incredible to see the rise of the Scouse accent," he adds, crediting the Netflix series Adolescence, starring and co-created by Stephen Graham, with accelerating the change.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "Stephen Graham really was the one who started the wave for Scouse actors," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "And then the likes of Jodie Comer and now you've got your Mike Nobles, your James Nelson-Joyces... and now your Adam Abbous.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "We're making waves for young Scouse talent." As for what's next, Abbou says the series has helped push his career forward and he has some "exciting projects lined up" which he can't speak about just yet.
sentences.article_title: The Scouse actor reaching new heights in Liverpool drama This City Is Ours

sentences.text: "I just want to do things that make me feel creatively fulfilled and mean something and have a voice." - The last episode of The City Is Ours season two airs on BBC One at 21:00 GMT.

sentences.text: Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top five places are occupied by  'big six' clubs.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Only second-placed Brighton , a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton , have muscled their way in.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: The six biggest clubs - Manchester United , Liverpool , Manchester City , Arsenal , Tottenham and Chelsea - now generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the division's other teams.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: BBC Sport breaks down how the finances of the big six have exploded, examines new trends and the impact on the transfer market, and asks how much it really matters.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Companies put their money where supporters are prepared to spend it.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: It is a simple fact of business in every country, a reality of football's food chain.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: In England, Liverpool , Arsenal and Manchester United traditionally dominated viewing figures, column inches, shirt sales and sponsorship.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Over the past 20 years they have been joined by Chelsea , Manchester City and Tottenham .
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: This group of clubs now generate so much money it is hard to imagine how they can fail in the long term - even factoring in short-term performance issues.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Let's look at how the gap has grown.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: We will use Everton , the only club not in the big six to be in the Premier League since its inception in 1992.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: This tells a tale of how even one of the league's founding members can be left trailing well behind.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: In 2009-10, the gap in revenues between the big-six average and Everton was £120m.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: In 2024-25, that gap had grown to £442m.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: So what has driven this huge escalation?
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: In large part it is the boom in international TV rights.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool , told BBC Sport that it has attracted companies prepared to pay large sums to be associated with the Premier League's top clubs.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "The big football brand clubs have global fanbases and that makes them very attractive to global commercial partners, especially for sponsorship and front-of-shirt deals," Maguire said.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "You combine that with the fact that the Premier League is broadcast to 190 different countries around the world, and especially the international audiences - that allows the clubs to negotiate very good prices." Only 10% of Everton 's revenue comes from commercial deals, while for the big six it is 45%.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: It means Everton , and other clubs in the league, are heavily reliant on broadcast income.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: It makes up 66% of their revenue.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: For Everton at least, this should change following the move to Hill Dickinson Stadium.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: But that is unlikely to be enough to stop the gap increasing.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: It has taken a few years, but Aston Villa and Newcastle have begun to increase their revenue.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: This is largely thanks to the financial rewards of Champions League football.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: But even Uefa has created a system which entrenches the position of the biggest clubs.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: When the European Super League plan was torpedoed, Uefa created a new financial deal called the value pillar.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: This reserves 35% of all Champions League revenues, or £713m, for the historically most successful clubs.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: At the end of the league phase last season City are estimated to have earned £37.9m from the value pillar, Liverpool £35.5m and Chelsea £33.3m.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Newcastle received only £13.6m.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: The good news for Villa is their coefficient has improved greatly, aided by last season's Europa League win.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Their value pillar is projected to be worth £25m this season.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: But that will still be less than the big six clubs in the competition.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: The cards are stacked against an ambitious club - not just domestically, but in Europe too.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Take a look at the financial trend of the big six and one thing becomes noticeable - Chelsea are beginning to fall behind.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: In the past two seasons, and for the first time in recent history, the Blues recorded the lowest revenues of the big six.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Not just by a small amount.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: They were £74m behind Tottenham , and £200m below Liverpool and Manchester City .
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: City's matchday income is the lowest, with the club's huge revenues largely due to commercial deals.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: City, however, have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, inflating the value by using "sham contracts" with sponsors.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: The club deny wrongdoing and have lodged an appealed against the verdict.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Chelsea 's problem is simple - seats.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Stamford Bridge has a capacity of only 40,000, with no easy scope for expansion.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: The rest of the big six have grounds which hold at least 60,000.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Chelsea generated an average spend per fan of £80 in 2024-25, the second highest in the league after Arsenal .
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Yet with 20,000 fewer tickets sold than their big six rivals, Chelsea 's total matchday revenues are dwarfed.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "Matchday spend has become increasingly important," Maguire said.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "There has been a flatlining of broadcast revenues, especially since 2017.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "As a consequence, clubs have had to look at alternative methods of increasing revenues, especially with costs both on the pitch and off pitch rising so fast." Matchday revenue has effectively stalled for Chelsea , rising only £16m over the past 10 years.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: United's has grown by £69m and Spurs , thanks to their new ground, by £85m.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: " Chelsea are far more reliant upon player sales," Maguire said.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "There is a growing divide because the global appeal is very much aligned with three or four clubs.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: " Arsenal have re-established themselves with their progress in the Champions League.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Manchester United are a brand in their own right.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: And Liverpool have expanded Anfield from 44,000 to 61,000, with many of those extra seats having gone to commercial." Chelsea 's successful player trading model has so far limited the impact.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: But there are signs that, financially at least, the big six could become the big five.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: You might recall that Villa and Newcastle were not fans of the old profit and sustainability rules (PSR).
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: PSR forced both clubs to sell some of their best players to balance the books.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: That has changed this season with squad-cost ratio (SCR).
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: There is a key difference with SCR, in that it allows a club to spend the money they generate on players.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: PSR limited losses so was more restrictive.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "This does make it a little easier for the likes of Villa and Newcastle to spend money," Maguire said.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "But it is still heavily weighted in favour of the big six.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "SCR is different to PSR rather than better.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: For some people, change is advantageous.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: For others, it isn't." The big six generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the other clubs.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: So they can spend hundreds of millions of pounds more on their squads.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: This makes the big six even more powerful in the transfer market.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "Look at the clubs who voted against SCR - Brighton , Brentford , Bournemouth , Crystal Palace , Fulham and Leeds ," Maguire said.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "It's very noticeable that those clubs have traditionally been very good at player sales, while they have tended to have lower matchday and commercial revenues." Most of the big six  - the outlier being Chelsea - are not remotely close to the Premier League's 85% SCR limit.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: If you give clubs more money to spend on transfers, the likelihood is they will do just that.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: And the numbers back that up.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Premier League clubs spent £3.5bn - not only a highest total for a summer window, but it almost smashed the record for a whole season, the £3.53bn set in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: The annual accounting cost of previous transfers, or amortisation, has been rising year on year.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "Over the course of the last decade, transfer amortisation has more than doubled and close to tripled," Maguire said.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "Which means that on average, clubs in the Premier League are now spending, or now have a cost which goes into their SCR calculations of just under £100m." Uefa fears that SCR will make matters worse, and have an inflationary impact across Europe.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: And you can see why it is concerned.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: In the summer 13 Premier League clubs broke their transfer record.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Brentford , Brighton , Palace, Leeds and Nottingham Forest all spent more than £40m on a player - unthinkable until recently.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: So we have learned that the big six have more money than ever, and the gap is so huge it is impossible for any other club to compete with them, financially at least.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: And this is an important point: other than Villa and Newcastle , the other clubs are not trying to compete with the big six.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Clubs like Brentford and Brighton have shown that smart models are just as effective as fat wallets.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: They sign the potential stars of the future, nurture them and then sell them to the big six.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Football's ecosystem recycles the big-six money through the transfer market.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: But it is a precarious business for these other clubs.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "The smaller clubs have to get it right on a more regular basis than the bigger clubs," Maguire said.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: "The big six can afford to make signings which are £60m and £70m, who turn out to be relative flops, and still have those players on high wages for several years." And this is perhaps the key point about the vast finances of the big six.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: The commercial power of the big six does not guarantee success.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: After all, United sit in the relegation zone.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Yet Mauricio Pochettino, their new manager, may well get the chance to revamp the squad despite the club spending £945m on players in the past five years.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: The richest clubs can try to spend their way out of trouble.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: But the rest of the league are only a couple of bad transfer windows from catastrophe.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: And that is the real gap between the big six and the rest.
sentences.article_title: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

sentences.text: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba has signalled his intention to run for president in the next elections In Uganda's military, even senior generals are finding that their rank offers little protection from the wrath of the country's powerful army chief.
sentences.article_title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

sentences.text: Over the past 15 months, at least a dozen generals and senior officers have been arrested under Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the son of President Yoweri Museveni, in a crackdown that has unsettled the military's top ranks.
sentences.article_title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

sentences.text: The arrests come amid growing political tensions over who will succeed Museveni, who has ruled Uganda for four decades.
sentences.article_title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

sentences.text: Gen Kainerugaba, 52, is widely seen as a potential successor, although his ambitions appear to be facing resistance within the ruling party.
sentences.article_title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

sentences.text: This week, he threatened Vice-President Jessica Alupo with dismissal and possible arrest, while suggesting he should take her position.
sentences.article_title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

sentences.text: The ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM) has, however, rejected reports that its senior leadership had rejected a proposal to back Gen Kainerugaba as the next president, describing the claims as "completely false".
sentences.article_title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

sentences.text: This has all fuelled speculation that the arrests are part of an effort to sideline military officers opposed to the general's presidential ambitions.
sentences.article_title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

sentences.text: At the centre of the tension are two powerful powerful institutions: the military, where Gen Kainerugaba wields considerable influence, and the NRM, where questions about his political ambitions appear to be dividing senior figures.

sentences.text: In the book, he tells the story of how his peers helped shape Wolverhampton into the city it is today.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "Today's diverse city did not simply appear.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: It has been shaped over decades by successive generations of people making Wolverhampton their home and contributing to its economic, social and cultural life," he said.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "A lot has been written about, and quite rightly so, the Windrush generation.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "I felt there wasn't much written about my generation.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: We were absent from the landscape." Pasvill Plummer came to live in Wolverhampton as a child in the 1960s For the book, the 74-year-old community activist interviewed 20 people who, like him, had Caribbean roots and grew up in Wolverhampton between the 1960s and 1980s.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: He reflected on what it was like settling into his new home in the city.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "Most people of my generation came to the UK on British Overseas Airways Corporation flights - we didn't come on a ship.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "When I came here, municipal accommodation wasn't accessible to our community.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "It was common for us to live in multi-occupancy houses.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: He added that the challenges he and his peers faced were often not something their parents could relate to.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "We are the children who came here, went to school, experienced discrimination and prejudice, and had to navigate those challenges as young people.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "Our parents came here to work, and they just worked, went to church and then went home.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: Plummer described his experiences as a child helped paved a smoother path for younger generations "The generation was not simply adapting to Wolverhampton.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: It was also helping to change Wolverhampton," he said.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: As they grew from children into young adults, venues such as The Queen's Ballroom, The Catacombs and Lafayette became known as "the place to be", where they mixed with other revellers.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: Plummer recalled: "Wolverhampton used to be a premier place for entertainment.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: Coaches used to come from Lichfield, Coventry, Birmingham and Stafford on a Monday night to go to The Queen's.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "Monday night was the night because we used to have lots of American stars, groups and artists who appeared on Top of the Pops performing there.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "At the Gaumont Cinema, I saw the Motown tour with Diana Ross and Stevie Wonder." Lanzel were a well-known dance group based in the city in the 1970s However, Plummer said getting into some of those nightclubs was not always easy, and having white friends often helped.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: While the book explores the barriers the generation had to overcome, he said that was only part of the story.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: It also focuses on a generation characterised by resilience, ambition, self-help and an increasing determination to create opportunities.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: "This is not simply a Black or Caribbean story.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: It is a Wolverhampton story," he added.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: He said his generation became part of the changing social fabric of the city.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: Over time, its members established careers, businesses and families.
sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: They also became involved in community and public life.

sentences.article_title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says

sentences.text: "I would say, in the round, this has been a complex visit.
sentences.article_title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says

sentences.article_title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says

sentences.text: "But the takeaway is that it's been very successful and I think the King has demonstrated his statecraft both by word and deed." Most of the King's visits outside the UK have seen him draw on some delicate diplomatic skills on behalf of his government.
sentences.article_title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says

sentences.article_title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says

sentences.article_title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says

sentences.article_title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says

sentences.article_title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says

sentences.article_title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says
